messages.subject: Error in DSM
parts:
Hello List,

 

When trying to run DSM after updating to Distance6.2 on an old dataset I get the following error message (fejl i = error in):

 

dsm.83<-dsm(ddf.obj=ddf.80,formula=Nhat~s(lon,lat),family=quasipoisson(link='log'),group=FALSE,engine='gam',convert.units=1,segment.data=sample.dat.83,observation.data=obs.dat.83)

Fejl i make.data(response, ddf.obj, segment.data, observation.data,  :

  Some observations are outside of detection function truncation!

 

The analysis did run in my previous version of Distance (6.1) and I can trace the error back to a change in the code for make.data.R on Github last October (https://github.com/dill/dsm/commit/3d6feb500f93f5d4d283ae691a285a4cd5c3b3f4). But this is dsm 2 and I ran dsm 1.0.3 earlier. It is some time since I last ran this project.

 

This leads me to the following questions:

 

It there a theoretically problem using truncated data in DSM or is it just the implementation in dsm 2.2.3?

Is there an easy fix (updating the dsm)?

Or should I modify my dataset (large) by eliminating the observations outside the truncation? (would rather avoid this).

 

BTW my dataset is multi-species boat-based bird observations binned in 4 transect bands and truncated. I run analysis for each species separately.

Med venlig hilsen / Kind regards,

Rasmus Bisschop-Larsen
Cand. Scient, biolog

www.niras.dk

r...@niras.dk

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in DSM
parts:
Hi Rasmus and listfolk,

Thanks for your concise problem definition and taking the time to find
exactly where the error appeared!

The error you describe is raised to ensure that only observations that
were used to fit the detection function are used to fit the spatial
model -- so that the same data are used to fit both model stages. Since
the truncation distance is used to form the width of the segment,
including observations at greater than the truncation seems like the
wrong thing to do as the effort will not be correctly accounted for in
the DSM.

What is odd to me is that you would have binned data, so all of the
distances should lie within the bins. If you are able to send me (off
list) the data/code from running Distance in debug mode, I can
investigate further.


All the best,
--dave

Hello Dave,

I am not sure I am allowed to send you the data. I will have to check up on that.

I have thought copied in the MRDS and DSM code below. The data is collected with observations placed in the individual transect bands A=0-50m, B=50-100m, C=100-200m and D=200-300. Some observation was placed in E=300+m. In order to import the observation to Distance I gave the observations the perpendicular distance equal to the midpoint of the transect band (25, 75, 150, 250 and 350). I decided to truncate at 300 since the observations given 350 could be 2000m or more away (likely they were closer). You can see this from the MRDS debug code. I ran different MRDS test but this is the one I used in the DSM I present. The DSM error arises setting the dsm.83. Hope it helps some. Oh, this is the in.r files.

Rasmus

MRDS:

source('C:\Distance\Distance 6\support.r')
source('C:\Distance\Distance 6\mrds.support.r')
install.distance.packages(dir='C:\Distance\Distance 6\RPackages\')
library(mrds)
file.create('C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\res.r')
file.create('C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\stat.r')

ddf.dat.80<-read.table(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\ddf.dat.r', header=TRUE, sep=' ', comment.char='')
res<-create.interval.data(ddf.dat.80$distance, c(0,50,100,200,300), 300)
ddf.dat.80<-cbind(ddf.dat.80, data.frame(distbegin=res$distbegin, distend=res$distend))
ddf.dat.80<-ddf.dat.80[(ddf.dat.80$distend<=300),]
rm(res)

ddf.80<-ddf(method='ds',dsmodel=~mcds(key='hr',formula=~seastate + flight),data=ddf.dat.80,meta.data=list(width=300,left=0,binned=T, breaks=c(0,50,100,200,300)))

ddf.summary.80<-summary(ddf.80)
sink(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\res.r',append=T)
cat(' Detection Fct/Summary ')
ddf.summary.80
sink()
ddf.gof.80<-ddf.gof(ddf.80, breaks=c(0,50,100,200,300))
sink(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\res.r',append=T)
cat(' Detection Fct/GOF ')
ddf.gof.80
sink()
win.metafile(filename='ddf.80.%02d.wmf',width=7,height=5,pointsize=12)
plot(ddf.80,breaks=c(0,50,100,200,300),lwd=2,lty=1,pch=1,cex=1)
dev.off()
sink(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\res.r',append=T)
cat(' Detection Fct/Plot: Detection Probability ')
sink()
write.stats.ddf('C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\stat.r',F,ddf.80, ddf.summary.80, ddf.gof.80)

region.dat.80<-read.table(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\region.dat.r', header=TRUE, sep=' ', comment.char='')
sample.dat.80<-read.table(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\sample.dat.r', header=TRUE, sep=' ', comment.char='')
obs.dat.80<-read.table(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\obs.dat.r', header=TRUE, sep=' ', comment.char='')

dht.80<-dht(ddf.80,region.dat.80,sample.dat.80,obs.dat.80,se=T,options=list(varflag=2,convert.units=.000001))
sink(file='C:\Users\rbl\AppData\Local\Temp\dst50810\res.r',append=T)
cat(' Density Estimates and associated quantities ')
print(dht.80,cor=T,bysample=T,vcmatrices=T)
sink()

parts:
Hi Rasmus (hi list!),

If you wish to get this analysis working in Distance I think you'll have
to re-import the data, but you have a few options in how you do this.

I think I was able to duplicate your bug using the dolphin example in R:

library(dsm)
library(Distance)

data(mexdolphins)

hr.model <- ds(mexdolphins$distdata, 7000, key ="hn",
adjustment = NULL, cutpoints=c(0,2000,4500,6000,7000))

mod1<-dsm(N~s(x,y), hr.model, mexdolphins$segdata, mexdolphins$obsdata)

The check that is implemented is to check that the column "distance" in
the observation data is not greater than the truncation. So here are
some options:

1) Remove the "distance" column in the observation data and re-import
into Distance -- this removes the check, giving you what you had before.
As I said in the previous e-mail, this will mean that the per-segment
effort is incorrect. In R one can simply perform (using the above as an
example:

mexdolphins$obsdata$distance <- NULL


2) Remove observations with observed distance larger than the
truncation. This is relatively simple in R (using the above as an example):

mexdolphins$obsdata <-
mexdolphins$obsdata[mexdolphins$obsdata$distance<=7000,])

You can then use write.csv() to write out the data.frame and re-import
into Distance (or carry on your analysis in R).


I hope this helps!


best,
--dave

Hello Dave (and list),

Thanks for the help. I think I understand my options now. But I have thought about this over the weekend and have a few follow-up questions.

If I use your method 1) will I then have a problem running further detection function fitting in Distance?
Why do the dsm abort after detecting observations outside the truncation? Why not just truncate the data before continuing? Also does it not actually (indirectly) truncate the data around line 30 in the make.data.R code?

I am not very good at coding R. I can roughly follow written code but have a hard time writing it myself at the moment.

Rasmus

-----Original Message-----
From: David Lawrence Miller [mailto:da...@ninepointeightone.net]

To: Rasmus Bisschop-Larsen (RBL); distance...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in DSM

Hi Rasmus (hi list!),

If you wish to get this analysis working in Distance I think you'll have to re-import the data, but you have a few options in how you do this.

I think I was able to duplicate your bug using the dolphin example in R:

library(dsm)
library(Distance)

data(mexdolphins)

hr.model <- ds(mexdolphins$distdata, 7000, key ="hn",
adjustment = NULL, cutpoints=c(0,2000,4500,6000,7000))

mod1<-dsm(N~s(x,y), hr.model, mexdolphins$segdata, mexdolphins$obsdata)

The check that is implemented is to check that the column "distance" in the observation data is not greater than the truncation. So here are some options:

1) Remove the "distance" column in the observation data and re-import into Distance -- this removes the check, giving you what you had before.
As I said in the previous e-mail, this will mean that the per-segment effort is incorrect. In R one can simply perform (using the above as an
example:

mexdolphins$obsdata$distance <- NULL


2) Remove observations with observed distance larger than the truncation. This is relatively simple in R (using the above as an example):

mexdolphins$obsdata <-
mexdolphins$obsdata[mexdolphins$obsdata$distance<=7000,])

You can then use write.csv() to write out the data.frame and re-import into Distance (or carry on your analysis in R).


I hope this helps!


best,
--dave

Hi Rasmus, listfolk,

To your follow-up questions:

Provided you continue to only perform binned analyses I believe that 1)
should continue to work. However, as I've said the results of your
models will be incorrect in some sense because the effort will be
incorrectly reported (so the offset of the DSM will be wrong; bear in
mind that the effort effectively acts as a multiplier on the other
effects in the DSM/GAM, so this can have a large effect on the results).

DSM fails at this point, rather than continuing while truncating, as my
view is that doing such an analysis is not advisable due to the effort
miscalculation.

The code at line 30 of make.data.R matches observations in the
observation frame to those in the predictions of probability of
detection, which as you say truncates the data (based on the object
identifiers).

I hope this helps, feel free to ask for clarification on any of the above.

best,
--dave
